headline: Math benchmarks saturate while real-world agent work trails well behind
outlook: Math is where progress has been most complete: the past year closed 95% of the remaining headroom there, FrontierMath crossed 90% in September, and GPT-6.1 Sol has just posted 100% on FrontierMath Tier 4. The harder test is turning that into sustained practical work, and here the picture is more mixed. The longest tasks models can handle have reached 17.4 hours with Claude Mythos Preview and are doubling roughly every 4.2 months, which on current trends points to work-week-length tasks around December, but the agents and real work category has closed only 32% of its headroom, with the Remote Labor Index at 20.8% and OSWorld 2 at 31.4%. Not everything is accelerating: the cheapest model scoring at least 80% on GPQA still costs $0.035 per million tokens, behind the trend that expected it under a cent by September, and Terminal-Bench and GeoBench have also stalled short of 90%. Treat the dates loosely, since past likely ranges caught the real date only 59% of the time, with a typical miss of five months, but the shape of the next year looks like longer autonomous tasks arriving well before broad competence at messy real-world jobs.
